The Anti-Defection Law was introduced by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985.
It aims to prevent political defections.
Deciding Authority:
• Speaker (Lok Sabha)
• Chairman (Rajya Sabha)
The Anti-Defection Law was introduced by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985.

items: Frequently asked: The Anti-Defection Law was enacted via the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act in 1985.
Note the deciding authority: Speaker in the Lok Sabha and Chairman in the Rajya Sabha.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Anti-Defection Law was brought into force by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985.
The primary purpose of the law is to prevent political defections.
The Speaker holds the deciding authority for defection cases in the Lok Sabha.
The Chairman holds the deciding authority for defection cases in the Rajya Sabha.
